data.body:
RED/GREEN and safety evidence before commit:
- RED: the final held-out oracle collected as one node and failed on current main with `AssertionError: loopback editor attempted reverse DNS for 127.0.0.1`; stack crossed `edit_workflow -> ThreadingHTTPServer -> HTTPServer.server_bind -> socket.getfqdn`.
- Held-out GREEN: the production-only fixer never saw or touched `tests/unit/workflow/test_editor.py`; after its two-file implementation, the restored oracle passed in 0.99s and completed a real `/workflow.bpmn` request.
- Mutation proof: defect-seeding `HTTPServer.server_bind` into the new subclass returned the unchanged oracle to RED at `socket.getfqdn`; restoring `TCPServer.server_bind` returned the production diff.
- Broader editor surface: 53 passed in 11.64s across editor, validation, and prompt-authoring modules. Worktree-venv lint passed (2023 files formatted; actionlint/zizmor/complexity/DCO clean), typecheck passed across 541 source files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Caller-dependency sweep: CLI, unit, and e2e callers all go through `edit_workflow` and consume only server handle, bound host/port, token, serving, and shutdown. `server_name` has no consumer in src/tests, so changing it from reverse-resolved text to the literal bound address is incidental.
- Safety: restores existing loopback behavior, adds no dependency/external call, weakens no test, and adds no skip/xfail. Construct sweep found no other production `ThreadingHTTPServer`/`HTTPServer` construction requiring this fix.
